meta.title: A frond made of smaller fronds
meta.description: Self-similarity WITHOUT recursion, which this library does not have: a subgraph may not reference itself, so a structure whose parts are smaller copies of the whole is spelled by applying one rule a fixed number of times and reading the unrolled result. The rule is `copyToPoints`, and what makes it a rule rather than a stamp is that it COMPOSES TRANSFORMS: a copy lands at `targetP + targetRot * (targetScale * sourceP)`, takes `targetRot * sourceRot`, and multiplies the scales. So a template carrying a per-point `rot` and a tapering `scale` is not decoration — it IS the production, and every point of the parent says where its child goes, which way it points and how much smaller it is. Here one template does all three levels. `rachis` is twenty points along a line; `scale` tapers them base to tip, and `rot` turns alternate points to alternate sides, so the template describes both a stem AND the placement of whatever is stamped on it. Stamping the template onto ITSELF gives the pinnae, stamping that result onto the template again gives the pinnules, and `topology: "keep"` re-emits the source polyline once per target so each copy arrives as a path rather than a loose cloud. Three levels is a choice, not a limit: a fourth is one more node and one more multiply on the count. The compounding is the point — a level-2 leaflet carries the product of two turns and two tapers, which is why the outline curves although nothing here computes a curve. What this graph cannot do is stop when the parts get small enough, or branch a different number of times at different places; that wants a loop with a settle condition rather than a fixed chain, and `basics-repeat-until-settled` is where that lives.
